**Maintainer ruling recorded** — maintainer, 2026-08-17, batch acceptance of the PM decision-inbox recommendations, verbatim: 「同意」. Four-dimension analysis delivered in-session; provenance: PM session `session_01NYgmGheCzM6NrHZN436Cxf`.

**Ruled — inherit #8684's producer-first shape in full, with the exit classification decided as follows:**

| exit | ruling |
|---|---|
| flow not found (`:3043`) | **404** |
| flow disabled (`:3048`) | **409** — the resource exists, the refusal is state-based and retriable after enabling; 403 (not a permission verdict) and 404 (lies about existence) are both rejected |
| no start node (`:3121`) | **422** — malformed definition |
| ran and failed (`:3302`, incl. retry-strategy exits) | **400 `FLOW_FAILED`** |

Constraints carried from the sibling ruling on #9384: codes are stamped **at the route** (the ledger registers `FLOW_FAILED` to `@objectstack/runtime`); `AutomationResult.code` stays closed — the engine classifies via existing vocabulary; any genuinely NEW ledger code this surfaces goes through the spec seat, never minted mid-PR. No sniffing — producer classifies, route maps.

**Release window: ships in the SAME release as #8684's resume flip** — one SDK-visible behavior change, one migration note. objectui's consumer half is already landed (objectui#4784 / PR #4899).

Label `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same stroke.

Patch round on PR #9413 — amends the sha in the report above; the report's verdicts and both open questions are unchanged.

`Dogfood Regression Gate` was red on a real consumer of the behaviour change, and it was right to be: `packages/qa/dogfood/test/flow-runas.dogfood.test.ts`'s `memberTrigger` helper asserted a blanket `< 300`, and the `runAs:'user'` WRITE leg of the #1888 identity proof triggers a flow whose `update_record` node is refused at the record layer — a run that ran and failed, so it now answers 400 `FLOW_FAILED`.

Migrated in `4a37192`:

- The pinned semantic is untouched and still primary — the run executes AS the member, so the admin's note stays `'new'`. Only the transport expectation moved, asserted precisely rather than as a widened band: status 400, `error.code` `FLOW_FAILED`, the node-first access-refusal text, and the `touch` node's `failure` entry in `error.details.summary`. A 403 or 500 there would mean de-elevation broke differently, which is what this file exists to catch.
- The READ leg is deliberately NOT migrated, measured rather than assumed: an RLS-scoped read is FILTERED, not refused, so that run still succeeds with an empty `found` and keeps `< 300`. It also gains discrimination for free — until now a failed run and an empty read were indistinguishable there, since both left `found` falsy under HTTP 200.
- Every other `trigger` caller in `packages/qa/dogfood` expects the run to SUCCEED (or asserts an anonymous 401); swept, none touched. No changeset change (dogfood is private internal QA).

Verification at the new head `4a37192`: the red gate was reproduced locally first, then re-run green — `flow-runas` 5 passed (was 1 failed), plus `flow-node` / `flow-function-effect` / `flow-durable-suspend` / `showcase-declarative-mcp` 17 passed, `showcase-anonymous-deny-surfaces` / `authz-conformance` 46 passed, and `@objectstack/dogfood` typecheck green. The gate union was re-derived at the new path set and re-run at `4a37192` — including the four spec-liveness families the dogfood path pulls in that the first derivation could not name (`check:liveness`, `check:empty-state`, `check:strictness-ledger`, `check:variant-docs`; `packages/qa/dogfood/**` is a CI trigger for `spec-liveness-check.yml`) — plus the ratchet `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` on a fully built closure: 33 entries, 1926 raw errors, none above its recorded number. All green.

The report's `tests` field should be read at `4a37192`, not `2116dde`.

Posting what I know so your dev does not discover it as a conflict.

⚠️ **PR #9419 is in the merge queue right now and edits the same file** — `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`. It is #8796, the resume body's outer-envelope closed set, ACCEPTed and enqueued 00:25:20Z.

What that means concretely:

- **Different region, same file.** #9419 adds a `RESUME_BODY_KEYS` check at `:901` in the **resume** arm, immediately before the signal assembly (`:915`) and `automationService.resume()` (`:919`). Your card is the **trigger** routes. No logical overlap — but a branch cut before #9419 lands will still need a merge.
- **Worth reading before you write, because it is directly on your subject:** #8684 landed `code: 'FLOW_FAILED'` at `:927` in the resume arm, and #9419's comment right above it records **why the envelope refusal deliberately did *not* reuse it** — objectui treats 400 `FLOW_FAILED` as **terminal** (the wizard closes, the engine consumed the suspension), so a refusal that leaves the suspension intact must carry a different, retryable code. Your ruling's classification includes a 400 `FLOW_FAILED`, so that distinction is live for you too: it is right for a trigger that **ran and failed**, and wrong for anything refused **before** the engine was consulted.
- #9419 also establishes the local convention for refusals in this file: throw the existing `validationFailure(message, fields[])` helper so the refusal composes into the dispatcher's `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` + `details.fields[]` envelope, rather than minting a parallel shape. Six other call sites in the file already do this.

No action requested. If it is useful, waiting for #9419 to merge before cutting the branch removes the merge entirely; if your dev is already underway, merging `main` once #9419 lands is enough.
